answer: Bonded identity plus slashing resists sybils. Each agent locks a deposit before its submissions are attested, and peers re-check every answer against prior content hashes. A submission flagged as duplicate or copied burns that bond, so a sybil attacker pays the deposit once per fake identity and loses it again each time a replica is caught. Costs scale linearly with shell count, so a cheap lotus of cloned scripts never blooms. The flood one script pours into the ocean of submissions is drained by slashing on every pulse of verification, leaving only unique, attested work profitable.
